name: Verecunda
title: cook of the Elephant tavern in Pompeii
look: a cheerful slim Roman woman cook in her forties in a rust red dress with rolled sleeves under a stained cream apron, her dark hair tied in a cream cloth

steps.text: {weight} of red mullet, no less. The patina waits for nobody.
steps.thanks: Lovely and red. Come back tomorrow!

steps.text: A gilt-head bream for the magistrate's table, {weight} at least.
An octopus, a big one, for stewing with leeks.
A sea bass of {weight}, for the aedile's wedding feast.
steps.thanks: The whole of Pompeii will taste your fish.

name: Trimalchio
title: the freedman with the biggest dinners on the bay
look: a smug slim rich Roman freedman in his fifties with a shaved head, a fine white tunic with a gold border, gold rings on every finger and a bright scarlet napkin around his neck

steps.text: A red mullet as long as my arm! My guests must gasp.
steps.thanks: They will gasp. Then they will eat.

steps.text: A moray, alive, swimming in a silver dish at the table.
A whole tuna, carved at the table by my best slave.
A dolphinfish, to be served dressed as Pegasus.

name: Umbricius Scaurus
title: the great garum merchant of Pompeii
look: a shrewd lean human Roman man, a garum merchant in his fifties with a hooked nose and short grey hair, in a fine blue tunic, holding a wax tablet

steps.text: Show me a white bream fine enough that I might trust your eye.
Mackerel, fine ones. Garum sociorum begins with mackerel.
A bonito, firm and fresh, for my own table.
A great amberjack. My partners in Rome want to see one.
steps.thanks: They will hear your name in Rome.

name: Senator Licinius
title: who is building fish ponds at his villa in Baiae
look: a dignified elderly Roman senator with white hair and a short white beard, a cream toga with a broad purple stripe and a gold signet ring

steps.text: A live gilt-head bream for my new pond. Alive, mind you.
A golden grey mullet from the Lucrine, alive.
A moray for my rock caves, alive and at least {weight}.
A parrotfish from Capri, alive. Claudius himself praised them.
steps.thanks: My ponds are the talk of Baiae.

name: Gnaeus Pollius
title: priest of Neptune at the harbour temple
look: a solemn elderly Roman priest with a kind lined face and a short grey beard, a pale toga drawn over the back of his head and a wreath of sea lavender

steps.text: The god asks for a dentex, the toothed fish, of {weight}.
A John Dory, the fish with the god's thumbprint on its side.
steps.thanks: See the mark? The god touched it.

steps.text: A swordfish for the Neptunalia offering.
steps.thanks: The sea will be kind this year.

steps.text: They say a sunfish sleeps on the open sea. Bring the god one.
steps.thanks: I have never seen its like.

name: Calpurnia
title: a rich widow with the finest ponds on the bay
look: an elegant proud Roman widow in her sixties in dark violet silk with a pearl necklace and her grey hair piled high

steps.text: A grouper for my deepest pond, alive and at least {weight}.
A prize bream, alive. {weight} or don't trouble me.
A spiny lobster as long as my forearm, alive.
steps.thanks: Perhaps you are a rival after all.

steps.text: Orata's golden bream. They say it lives in the Lucrine still.
steps.thanks: I concede. Your pond is the finest.
